meta.status: MEASURED unless a row says DESIGNED
meta.units: px = reference pixels; D = ball diameter in the reference = 928.2 px; frac_D = px / D; arc angles on the sphere in degrees
meta.image_frame: x right, y down, origin top-left pixel corner
meta.image_angle: degrees CCW from the 3 o'clock direction about the ball centre, y up (90 = 12 o'clock, 180 = 9 o'clock, 270 = 6 o'clock)
meta.camera_frame: X right, Y up, Z toward the camera; lat/lon: lat from the X-Z plane toward +Y, lon from +Z (facing the camera) toward +X (right)
meta.back_projection: orthographic about the silhouette circle (centre 627.38, 628.92; R 464.11 px) -- see camera.projection
meta.trace_file: WorkFiles/smokebomb/reference_metrology/sb_trace.json (measurement use only; the build must not read it or the reference pixels)

silhouette.edge_rule: half-maximum between the background (stored lum 0.996) and the cloth just inside the rim (0.162)

centre_px.method: geometric circle fit to 3600 radial edge samples

circularity_rms_dev.method: rms radial deviation from the fitted circle

ellipse_axes_px.method: direct LSQ ellipse; long axis along image angle 125 deg (upper-left to lower-right), ratio 1.0198

flattening.method: sector mean radius vs fitted R

value: 88 deg (top, at the whorl): local +14.9 px = +3.2 %R over ~6 deg

outline_bumpiness.method: radius minus its n<=6 Fourier reconstruction

strip_edge_steps.method: radius jumps > 4 px within 0.5 deg of arc

thread_tips_past_outline.tol: max <= 9 px; no thread longer than 10 px beyond the outline
thread_tips_past_outline.note: only fibre fuzz and one small hook (T4, image angle ~155 deg) break the outline; no loose thread hangs off the ball

no_features: no tear, cut, scorch or dirt
no free strip end anywhere on the visible side

projection.tol: use orthographic for the comparison render
projection.method: a centred sphere's outline is a circle at every focal length and the reference has no other perspective cue; the spec's sphere positions were back-projected orthographically, so an orthographic camera reproduces them exactly. With a 100 mm FF lens a point 45 deg from the view axis lands 9 % R further out than orthographic, with 200 mm 4.7 % R -- so do not mix a perspective camera with these numbers.

elevation.method: a sphere on a seamless white ground has no horizon, no contact shadow and no ground plane, so elevation is not measurable. The strip layout is specified in the camera frame; rendering at elevation 0 with the ball oriented as specified IS the reference view.

alternative_if_top_whorl_is_world_up.status: DERIVED convenience, not a second measurement

background.method: all four corners and rings 25..240 px outside the ball: mean 0.9960, std 0.002; uniform, no gradient, no shadow, no ground line

camera.focal_length_note: any lens >= 85 mm FF also explains the outline; not measurable

lighting.method: 16 px blocks, 75th percentile of linear luminance (the lit top of the cloth, crevices excluded), fitted on the sphere normals

key.unit: deg (camera frame; az + = right, el + = up)
key.method: key+fill+ambient Lambert fit, alternating grid search

fill.method: same fit; lights the LEFT limb from the left-rear

softness.value: large soft sources: no terminator line, no cast shadow, shading ramps smoothly (wrap ~0.1); brightest visible normal (0.22, 0.89, 0.40), darkest (-0.09, -0.56, 0.82), max/min 4.15

quadrant_targets_lin.tol: each +-15 % after the render's overall exposure is matched at the centre
quadrant_targets_lin.method: same block statistic -- measure the builder's render the same way

specular.value: none: no glossy hot spot anywhere; highlights are only fibre/rim sparkle (see cloth.sheen)
specular.method: p99.9 of the disc is 0.615 stored and lives on fibres and rolled edges

albedo_lum_lin.method: region mean linear luminance / modelled irradiance, irradiance scaled so a perfect white facing the key reads 1.0 (the backdrop reads 0.996). If the backdrop was lit hotter than the ball (common), the true albedo is higher; 0.043 matches the kunai wrap's dark cotton (~0.04).

chromaticity_lin.method: pooled region means (all strips agree within r 0.375-0.386)

saturation_hsv.method: region means 0.113..0.160 (darker regions read slightly more saturated)

band_to_band.value: no strip-to-strip colour difference beyond lighting: chromaticity identical within 1.5 %; shading-normalised luminance spread (cv 0.22) follows the lighting-model residual (left limb reads bright, bottom reads dark), not the strips
band_to_band.tol: build: one BC for all strips, per-strip variation <= 5 %

pixel_targets_srgb.method: what the viewer sees: the render of the shipped asset must reproduce these under the specified camera and light

construction.value: plain-weave cotton-like tape, warp-faced: the visible texture is striations ALONG each strip; the cross (weft) structure is a faint irregular grid
construction.method: FFT of 64 px patches in 7 strips: 39-58 % of texture power within +-20 deg of the along-strip lines, 13-20 % across

warp_pitch.method: dominant spectral peak per patch: A 4.3/4.1, B 4.0, C 3.4, U 3.6, W 3.2, X 5.5, rim 3.0-3.9

weft.value: no stable period (3..18 px across patches); read as irregular cross-dots at ~2x the warp pitch

persistent_streaks.method: warp lines averaged 120-220 px along the strip: A 6.6, B 7.7, C 5.0, X 9.8 per 100 px; these are the only 'slub'-like features

slubs.value: no distinct slubs (thick knots) are resolvable -- do not add them beyond the persistent streaks

sheen.method: pixels > 3x the 6-px local median: fibre sparkle, warm light grey (tinted by the dye, not white), thinning toward the limb; no broad sheen lobe

cloth.roughness_reading: matte cloth: no specular lobe; sparkle comes from fibre ends and rolled edges

step_height.method: direct: radius jumps where strip edges cross the outline (12 jumps >= 4 px, median 5.7); consistent with the shading: rim highlight 4..8 px wide on the over strip, crevice 2.5..3.5 px on the under strip

edge_signature.tol: rim 0.4..1.2 log brighter; crevice 0.3..0.65 log darker
edge_signature.unit: px offsets across the edge (sign = normal of the traced polyline)
edge_signature.method: mean aligned cross profile along each edge
edge_signature.reading: every over-strip edge reads as a ROLLED, fuzzy rim 1.5-3x brighter than the strip, with an occlusion crevice 30-47 % darker on the strip beneath

fray_amplitude.method: edge position jitter about a 41-px running median, per edge: WLO 1.99, WUP 1.00, BLO 1.72, BUP 1.87, ALO 0.92, CLO 1.38, CUP 1.14, L3L 2.55, UA 1.71

fray_wavelength.method: 2 / zero-crossing rate of the jitter: WLO 12.2, WUP 15.2, BLO 12.3, BUP 10.8, ALO 8.8, CLO 9.4, CUP 13.2, L3L 11.9, UA 8.4

loose_threads.where: hangs from W's lower edge at (801,703) down over A
loose_threads.shape: curly, forks ~12 px from the tip

loose_threads.where: hangs from W's lower edge at (936,783) down over A
short fibre curl lying on A
hook on the outline at the left

loose_thread_count.method: visual scan + thin-ridge detector (strip-crossing bright ridges)

twisted_section.reading: the strip is seen edge-on / rolled for ~290 px: a raised double rim 6-15 px wide, then it opens

the great circles through B's edges return to the limb at 192.0 / 206.9 deg, inside C's entry band 198..221 deg

top.method: apex of the whorl V-gap and the convergence of R2/R3/R_in (from the left), U0..U4 (from below), U5/UF (to the right); the whorl V-gap is ~90 px long and ~20 px wide at its open end

bottom.value: at or just behind the bottom outline, image angle 265..280 deg; not visible
bottom.method: convergence of the D family edges

far_side.status: DESIGNED -- NOT MEASURED. The reference shows one hemisphere (orthographic: exactly half the ball). Nothing below is evidence.
proposal: Continue every visible strip on its own path across the back; add no strip that cannot be traced from a visible one.

A and W leave the right limb at 330..349 deg heading down-right; the great circles through their edges return to the visible side at 147..164 deg, where A and W have already passed under R_in/R2 at the upper-left. On the back run A and W from the right limb under the bottom-back and up over the back to the upper-left limb, closing each loop at the measured widths (+-15 %).

B and C are one strip on the front (INFERRED, see inferred_continuity): close its loop across the back from the right limb (12..26 deg) to the lower-left limb (198..221 deg), widening from 0.173 D at B's end to 0.227 D at C's end.
X continues under B/W over the back and ends tucked under the D family near the bottom convergence.

The U family and R family continue through the top whorl and down the back as meridian-like strips that converge on the bottom whorl, which sits 10..20 deg behind the bottom outline (sphere ~ (0.05, -0.97, -0.25)).
Keep the same crossing style as the front: roughly half of the crossings with W/A-like strips on top; step height, fray, sparkle and colour identical to the front.
The tape's free end, if modelled at all, is TUCKED under a strip on the back -- no visible flap, no knot, no fuse, no tag (the front shows none).
far_side.acceptance: a back view must read as the same object: same strip widths (0.04..0.24 D), a whorl at each pole, no feature the front lacks

cannot_show: the ball's real size (all lengths are fractions of D)
which of R_in/R2/R3 is on top of which
true tape thickness beyond the silhouette steps
acceptance_checks: render SM_SmokeBomb from the BAKED maps with an orthographic camera (scale 1.351 D per frame width), 1254x1254, backdrop 0.996, lights per 'lighting'
outline: circle fit within +-1 % D, rms dev 0.8..1.8 % R, 8..16 steps >= 4 px, no thread beyond 9 px
strips: every strip in 'strips' present, width within tolerance, entering/leaving at the listed limb angles +-6 deg, every 'crossings' row in the stated order
pixel targets: disc p10/p50/p90 stored luminance within +-12 %; quadrant lighting ratios within +-15 %
look first: overlay the render on the reference at 50 % and flip; any strip, whorl gap, twisted section or thread that reads differently is a failure even if the numbers pass
